solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ten years, not extremely degenerate

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the outer letters of not are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of not

explanation.surface: A whole decade spent not quite in utter debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not extremely' looks like a qualifier meaning 'not very', but it asks for the extremes of NOT: its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral or cultural decline marked by self-indulgence, so it is a synonym for degenerate.

clue.text: Closing section is not applicable in dossier

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents
N/A, the standard abbreviation on forms

explanation.surface: An official notes that the closing part of a report is marked N/A in the file.
explanation.walkthrough: N/A is the tick-box abbreviation on forms; 'is' is only a link word between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing section of a piece of music or a show.

clue.text: Great deal, including fine attic space

parts.note: a lot is a great deal
F = fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line: a bargain that comes with a fine attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great deal' sounds like a bargain but just means 'a lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the roof space of a house, reached by a hatch or ladder, goes by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Queen referring to gain in an unusual way

indicators.note: the letters of 'gain' are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: re = regarding, as in a letter heading
letters of GAIN rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about the Queen profiting by odd means.
explanation.walkthrough: Regina is Latin for queen, the R in ER on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the Latin title of a reigning queen.

clue.text: It may help to remember version adapted to accommodate you

indicators.note: to accommodate means to make room for, so the rearranged letters hold another inside
adapted means altered to suit, so the letters of version are rearranged

parts.note: U is text-speak for you, sounding the same

explanation.surface: A writer reworks a version of a memoir to suit the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges VERSION to SOVENIR, and 'to accommodate' takes U (you) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a keepsake bought or kept as a reminder of a place or event.

clue.text: Cheers up over drink, with minimum of ice included, in part of large building

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next
in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: ta is a British informal word for thank you, like cheers

indicators.note: included means put inside, so the letter goes into the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, a single letter, its first

parts.note: first letter of ice

explanation.surface: A toast is raised over a rum, with just a little ice, in a grand building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TA to AT, set 'over' RIUM: 'minimum of' takes I from ice, and 'included' puts it into RUM. Ta and cheers both mean thanks in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central hall, often glass-roofed and several storeys high, within a large building.

clue.text: Brilliant to incorporate Mike's highest point of achievement

parts.note: ace = excellent, brilliant
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Praise for Mike's career peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in Mike's is only surface glue; M sits inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from the Greek for 'point', it names the very summit of anything, especially achievement.

clue.text: Not quite epic — large book summary

parts.note: EPIC without its last letter
a tome is a big, heavy book

explanation.surface: A review sneering that a big book falls short of epic.
explanation.walkthrough: Epitome is used here in its older sense of an abstract or summary, not 'perfect example'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a summary or abstract of a written work.

clue.text: Device for measuring spirits — choose one carefully to begin with

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I = one, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: only the beginning, the first letter, of 'carefully' is taken

parts.note: first letter of CAREFULLY

explanation.surface: Advice to a bar-worker to pick a measure with care.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is the British pub device fixed to an upside-down bottle that dispenses an exact measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is the trade name for the measuring tap on spirit bottles in British bars.

clue.text: Separate answer section

parts.note: A = answer, as in Q and A
section, as in one portion of a paper

explanation.surface: An exam instruction to answer one section separately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' is an adjective here, as in 'kept apart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, 'kept apart' and 'kept separate' mean the same thing, so the swap works.

clue.text: Bill ready to sing?

definitions.meaning: bill in the commercial sense, a request for payment
a singer ready to perform is said to be in good voice; here the answer splits into two words

explanation.surface: A man called Bill warming up to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name, a singer; the second meaning splits the answer into IN VOICE, which the question mark flags as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent for goods or work.

clue.text: Discomfort seeing letters, we hear — practise

indicators.note: the letters are heard, not seen, giving their sound

parts.note: the letter I in the plural, said out loud
to train is to practise

explanation.surface: A complaint about the discomfort of reading, then an instruction to practise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' is not any letters but specifically the letter I, twice, which sounds like EYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is discomfort in the eyes from seeing too hard or too long.

clue.text: Attempt to pack in a singlet is farce

indicators.note: the word for attempt packs the other words inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
A + VEST, a vest being a singlet

explanation.surface: Someone trying to cram a sleeveless top into a bag, a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, a singlet, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque imitation, a farce.

clue.text: Slander most ugly, despicable, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the first letter of every one of the words

parts.note: the first letters of most, ugly and despicable

explanation.surface: Smears are the ugliest and most contemptible thing of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' looks like 'above all', but it takes the first letter of each of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw mud is to sling damaging accusations, so mud is figurative slander or defamation.

clue.text: Pay no regard to deduction from full price

definitions.meaning: verb sense: to set aside or disregard
noun sense: money taken off the price

explanation.surface: A shopper told to ignore the reduction from the full price.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a verb, the second a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Discount means both to disregard and a price reduction.

clue.text: Rebuke, however you look at it

indicators.note: however you look at it means from either side, so the answer reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: a click of the tongue in mild reproof

explanation.surface: A reprimand is a reprimand, whichever way you see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'however you look at it' tells you the answer is the same read either way. Tut is the click of the tongue made in disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut is to make a clicking sound of disapproval, a mild reproof or scolding.

clue.text: Vegetable change I propose initially

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns or leaves turn

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the first letter of propose

parts.note: first letter of propose

explanation.surface: A cook suggests swapping in a different vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes P from propose, after TURN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a root vegetable with white flesh, grown for its swollen root.

clue.text: Equipment mixed up as a trap?

indicators.note: the letters that follow are mixed into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some kit has been set up as a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of 'mixed up', but the anagram needs its letters; only 'mixed' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the set of tools or machines used for a job, as in breathing or laboratory gear.

clue.text: Steal from large building housing female by river

indicators.note: 'by' means next to, as in a house by the sea

parts.note: a pile is a large, grand building
F = female
R = river, as on maps

explanation.surface: A plan to steal from a riverside mansion where a woman lives.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile is a jokey British word for a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with a flavour of petty theft: taking small items on the sly.

clue.text: Showy stuff put in selection boxes

indicators.note: the phrase boxes the answer inside it

parts.note: inside puT IN SELection

explanation.surface: Glitzy things packed into a selection box, a Christmas scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' is a verb, not the selection boxes of chocolates at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittery decoration, showy but cheap.

clue.text: After shake-up a ruler's very strange

indicators.note: the letters that follow have been shaken into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A political comment: after a government reshuffle the leader is behaving oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of ruler's supplies the S, and 'shake-up' sounds like a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means bizarre, dreamlike, very strange.

clue.text: Cereal close to oats in the past

indicators.note: the close, the last letter, of 'oats' is taken

parts.note: last letter of OATS
ago = in the past

explanation.surface: A food historian saying a cereal once came close to oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it means the end of 'oats'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain from palm pith, used like a cereal in puddings.

clue.text: Part of Robin Goodfellow's game

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow

parts.note: inside roBIN GOodfellow's

explanation.surface: A question about which game belongs to Robin Goodfellow, the folklore sprite Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck; the name is only there to carry the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance played with numbered cards.

clue.text: Centre of operations of inferior quality

definitions.meaning: the headquarters that operations are run from, as for an army
low-grade, as in the metals alchemists tried to turn to gold

explanation.surface: A complaint that headquarters is shoddy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a noun, the second an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Base is both a headquarters and an adjective for low or inferior.

clue.text: Remorse of fellowship, taking time to replace diamonds

indicators.note: taking means bringing in, so the word takes on a new letter
the new letter replaces the old one, a swap

parts.note: a guild is an association or fellowship of tradespeople
D is the card abbreviation for the suit of diamonds

explanation.surface: A jewellers' guild feels sorry once a watch is substituted for its diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' T (time) 'to replace' D (diamonds) turns GUILD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt is the feeling of having done wrong, so it is a close synonym for regret or contrition.

clue.text: English at back of ship referring to One Direction?

parts.note: E = English
astern means at or toward the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: An English fan at the back of a boat talking about the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is the boy band, but the definition means literally one compass direction, east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means relating to the east, one of the four compass directions.
